newsitem.title: UGANDA: U.S. team arrives in Uganda on Zaire mission.
newsitem.headline: U.S. team arrives in Uganda on Zaire mission.

text.p: A U.S. assessment team led by an army general arrived in Uganda's capital on Wednesday to investigate conditions for any U.S. involvement in a multinational force for Zaire.

The team was expected to visit southwest Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania and possible centres in eastern Zaire for the multinational humanitarian operation, Western diplomats and Ugandan officials said.
The team of more than 40 was led by U.S. army Major-General Edward Smith, commander of the Southern European Task Force based in Vicenza, Italy, the U.S. Information Service said.

"The team is travelling within the region to conduct a technical survey to determine the operational requirements for providing greater support to humanitarian activities in eastern Zaire," it said in a statement.

A spokesman at Uganda's foreign ministry told Reuters the Ugandan government had opened Entebbe Airport, on the shores of Lake Victoria, to the international community for logistics and other humanitarian activities related to the Zairean crisis.

Washington has come under pressure to send troops as part of a multinational intervention force under Canadian leadership to help more than a million people -- long-term Rwandan and Burundian refugees as well as Zaireans -- cut off from all aid by the recent fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops.
